## Failure paths and arms (fill in)

Tested source `560d5fb88c142a17d73aeef135aff92f5f58c613` includes the verified
base merge and the consumer bookkeeping fix. The executable was built from its
clean isolated Git archive with `-trimpath -buildvcs=false`; its SHA-256 is
`e179fe0f87ac4852f0617c583a466bca718cd0e0e54afb44e4af5fe59bbd95e9`.
All native services, identities, credentials and fault targets were synthetic,
inside one exclusively owned disposable outer VM. Two source/executable copies
and separate VM state directories consumed one shared cache.

| Native arm | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Partial initialization | First startup returned nonzero and global running remained false; an APT-only VM still completed cloud-init, selected-file checks and teardown. Explicit fixture retries and synthetic origin CA trust completed initialization; unsuccessful attempts were preserved. |
| Missing management material | Individually removed Harbor admin/database passwords, Pulp admin/settings secrets and the CA private key. All five real APT consumer VMs provisioned, listed their exact registration and tore down with no remaining domain, target or registration. The missing file stayed absent through cleanup; container identity/start time and physical configuration hashes/mtimes stayed unchanged. Restored ServiceState contents matched the pre-arm state. |
| Failed provisioning cleanup | For each of those five missing-file states, an explicitly disclosed executable shim made native qemu-img overlay creation return 73 after registration. Each refusal contained the intended sentinel and left no pending claim or domain. This is injected failure, not an observed spontaneous qemu-img failure. |
| Explicit release and repeat teardown | Unconfirmed release refused specifically for missing interruption confirmation in every arm. Confirmed exact release succeeded while the admin password was absent. Repeating CLI down after successful deletion returned the expected no-target refusal and preserved absence; this is not a claim that repeated CLI down exits zero. |
| Shared startup, readonly and cancellation | Independent startup processes retained all 11 container identities/start times and physical configuration. Repeated readonly probes and a real SIGTERM during an owned-host loopback delay preserved state/lifecycle; the delay was removed and readiness recovered. |
| Legacy and descriptor-only policy | Valid descriptor-stripped state with denied Harbor administration still served APT/OCI without backfill. Missing OCI policy refused before domain creation; adding its immutable descriptor allowed consumption without recreation or physical fingerprint change. |
| Management denied, data ready | Real Harbor management HTTP 401 remained a failed administrative observation while proven APT/RPM/OCI consumers succeeded. Management startup refused the wrong credential without implicit repair. |
| APT outage | Required APT and the mixed topology union refused before domain creation; OCI-only consumption succeeded. With a live consumer, repair/down/confirmed-purge refused specifically at the consumer gate. Explicit APT restoration recovered readiness. |
| Management ready, data denied | Making the synthetic Harbor project private retained authenticated management/native health, refused OCI consumption, and still allowed APT. Restoring public access recovered the data probe. |
| Pulp outage | Required RPM refused before creation while APT consumption succeeded. Explicit Pulp restart recovered native health and data readiness. |
| Fresh mixed topology | Two new nodes passed syntax, check/diff, apply, 4/4 verify rows with no failures/skips, and second apply changed=0 on both. Actual groups and selected/unselected guest configuration files were asserted. Both domains were removed. |

APT used an immutable public Ubuntu package with verified SHA-256; Pulp served
native RPM metadata and the synthetic fixture payload; OCI used an immutable
BusyBox manifest and its real anonymous Bearer flow. A native Docker pull and
guest APT package retrieval also completed. The matrix retained instance and
generation identity through the controlled faults and recovery.

The first missing-admin attempt passed provisioning, release and teardown, then
the external harness incorrectly compared services.json mtime across expected
consumer registration writes. Its output/result were preserved. The corrected
oracle compares physical files independently and requires the complete restored
ServiceState contents to match; all five arms and the complete matrix/chain were
then rerun without changing production source or any spec expectation.

Current-source local checks passed: 896 scoped tests/subtests, 28 selected CLI
tests/subtests, zero skips, build-all, scoped vet and golangci-lint 2.12.1.
Three archived old-constructor controls failed specifically at the intended
teardown, listing and confirmed-release assertions. Native strace cancellation
tests executed in the local receipt rather than being skipped.

The additional known-secret scan covered 185 output/JSON/Markdown files,
including the superseded fixture attempt, against five runtime secret/private-CA
sources and the wrong-admin sentinel in raw, Basic-auth and JSON-escaped forms:
zero matches. Fixture source definitions were outside that output scan.
After capture, all nested domains were absent; pilot removed the owned outer VM,
its overlay/SSH-key directory and its target state. Unrelated VMs and operational
caches were outside the mutation boundary.
